messages:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT PAGER: HIGH_LATENCY_KV_CACHE — Triggered for inference-prod-eu-west-1 at 2026-03-14T22:00:00Z. Priority: P1. Symptoms: sustained token generation latency spikes 4-6x, increased 502/504 errors for dedicated customers. Pager: @oncall.

sanjay: paging oncall — seeing continuous-batching queues explode and KV cache size skyrocketing on tp-shard-*-eu-west-1. NCCL stalls showing up in logs, GPUs waiting on allreduce. 90% of affected requests are long-context chat flows. :rotating_light:

ashley: confirmed. perf cliff started ~21:50Z. metrics: token latency p99 jumped from 120ms -> 750ms, error rate for route /v1/generate up to 7%. Dedicated customer Glyph reporting tail latency timeouts. Switching to incident channel.

julia: quick ask — do we have an automated fallback to local KV reads when shard map is imbalanced? I think that path didn't trigger because batching aggregated across shard owners.

kevin: digging logs now. NCCL error repeating: "NCCL WARN Multiple calls to ncclCommInitRank for same pair" followed by timeout on allreduce. Looks like uneven partitioning: one tensor-parallel service instance got >60% of KV keys for active prefixes.

ashley: hypothesis: a recent change to shard assignment (rolling hash tweak) + continuous batching increased prefix sharing across requests, amplifying a corner where one TP replica becomes hot. Hot replica then causes NCCL handshake/backpressure -> system-wide stall.

mike_oncall: acknowledging. taking lead and will coordinate mitigations. immediate goals: 1) reduce customer impact 2) restore steady throughput 3) collect root cause artifacts.

pagerduty-bot: INC ACK by mike_oncall at 2026-03-14T22:04:03Z.

sanjay: mitigation plan I'm pushing now: 1) disable continuous batching on the affected service cluster (eu-west-1) 2) reduce target batch size to 8 3) enable aggressive kv-eviction policy for long-tail prefixes 4) rollout a temp shard-map rollback to previous hashing function.

ashley: rolling a config hotfix to inference-kv-service via ssm patch. command I'm using:

```
curl -X PATCH https://infra.api.redwood.internal/configs/inference-kv-service \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \n  -d '{"continuous_batching": false, "batch_target": 8, "kv_eviction_ms": 300000}'
```

ashley: applying now to eu-west-1 only.

ops-bot: deploy job started: config-patch/inference-kv-service@eu-west-1. JobID: job_20260314_2206. Rolling update: 5 pods -> maxUnavailable 2.

kevin: I also pushed a temporary workaround to the TP coordinator: force local-only KV read if a shard owner has >40% of active prefixes. patch:

```
if (owner_load_fraction > 0.4) { fallback_to_local = true; }
```

kevin: pushing rollout to tp-shard-workers now. kubectl commands:

```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/tp-shard-worker-eu-west-1
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=tp-shard-worker -w
```

julia: logs from one of the bad pods (tp-shard-worker-7c9b4):

```
[22:02:11Z] NCCL WARN : recv timeout waiting for allreduce, rank 3->0 timeout
[22:02:12Z] KV_CACHE: owner_load_fraction=0.62, pending_batches=128
[22:02:12Z] BATCHER: queue_depth=2048, avg_batch_size=42
```

ashley: glyph ops SRE reporting 503s between 21:55-22:05Z for large chat jobs. We sent an automated outage notification to Glyph (customers@glyph-app.com) mentioning degraded performance and mitigation in progress.

customer-success-bot: Notification sent to Glyph: "We're investigating higher latencies in EU; mitigations underway. Expected service restoration within 30-45 minutes." Ticket created: CS-7842.

mike_oncall: monitoring the effects of disabling continuous batching. If p99 and errors drop within 5-10 minutes, we'll consider a staggered rollout to remaining regions.

sanjay: initial numbers after patch (22:12Z): batcher queue depth down from 2048 -> 320, avg_batch_size down 42 -> 10, p99 token latency decreased ~60% on affected pods. Error rate down to ~1.8%.

kevin: NCCL warnings are reduced but not gone. I suspect some long-lived connections still hold onto stale shard maps. Plan: graceful pod restart for top-3 hot replicas to force fresh shard negotiation and drop stale allreduce groups.

ashley: scheduling rolling restart of hot pods with 30s spacing.

ops-bot: rollout restart started: tp-shard-worker-eu-west-1 pods rotating. 3 / 5 restarted.

julia: I'm collecting heap dump + KV index snapshot from one hot pod and uploading to s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/1868604321/ for RCA.

kevin: after restarts, NCCL warnings resolved. Metrics at 22:36Z: p99 token latency approaching baseline (~160ms), errors ~0.8%. kv cache size stabilized.

mike_oncall: declaring impact reduced but still watching for regressions. Moving incident to partial mitigation. I'll keep monitoring for an hour and then handoff to oncall-next for postmortem.

ashley: action items for post-incident: 1) revert the recent shard-hash change and add e2e test for uneven partition scenarios 2) add a safety valve to disable cross-shard batching in presence of owner_load_fraction > 0.3 3) improve alerting to detect rapidly growing avg_batch_size on a per-shard basis.

sanjay: customer follow-up: Glyph wants timeline and config docs. assigning CS->engr liaison to supply logs and mitigations. Ticket CS-7842 updated with mitigation notes and artifacts link.

mike_oncall: handing off to night-oncall (kevin) at 23:00Z for watch; I'll prepare an incident summary for the SRE rotation. Key blame: interaction of continuous batching + changed shard assignment -> uneven owner load -> NCCL stalls. Severity: P1->P2 after mitigation. Next: postmortem in #postmortems, draft in progress.

kevin: taking handoff. I'll keep this thread pinned and will post a short timeline + RCA draft by 08:00Z tomorrow.

pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT: status changed to INVESTIGATING -> MONITORED. Last update 2026-03-14T23:00:02Z.

mike_oncall: final notes before handoff: saved hot pod core dumps, disabled continuous batching globally for eu-west-1 until follow-up deploy, notified affected customers, created postmortem checklist. Good work team. :tada:

kevin: acknowledged. leaving monitoring dashboards open. any on-call should @kevin or @sanjay for quick escalation.
